subject: Request: bespoke SLA remedy & term discount for Valence.ai
summary: Customer requests a non-standard SLA remedy structure (higher uptime target + capped service credit) in exchange for a 2-year committed discount. Deal desk recommends limited concession; seeking executive approval for credit cap and discount.
messages:
From: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@valence.ai>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@valence.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA ask — 99.995% target + capped credits (Valence renewals)

Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re close on commercials — Procurement asked me to surface one remaining ask on reliability before we sign. Valence is willing to commit to a 2-year term and a material volume guarantee if Redwood will accept: 1) a 99.995% uptime target for our production inference workload (multi-region) and 2) a capped remedy (service credits not to exceed 3 months of fees per incident, and an annual cap of 6 months of fees).

We know that’s outside standard language but we’ll trade it for an upfront 15% ARR discount on committed usage and a 6-month prepayment. Attached is our redline and a short commercial summary. Can you confirm whether this is something Redwood can entertain, and what approvals would be required?

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Reynolds
Head of Infrastructure — Valence.ai
Attachment: valence_sla_redline_v3.pdf (pdf, 48 KB)

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
To: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@valence.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask — 99.995% target + capped credits (Valence renewals)

Sam — thanks for the clear ask and the redline. I’ve looped in Marissa (Deal Desk) and Ben (Sales Ops) to scope commercial impact and routing implications. High level: we can consider a tailored remedy if we can bound our exposure (max credit liability) and add operational protections (routing fallback, regional failover plan).

Marissa / Ben — can you please: 1) confirm the financial exposure if we accept the credit caps Sam proposes; 2) recommend a pricing offset (Marissa’s team usually models this as a blended discount); and 3) flag whether this requires exec signoff (I suspect yes for the credit cap deviation). I’ll also ask Ops to confirm feasibility.

Sam — I’ll get back with a recommended path within 48 hours.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Principal Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@valence.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask — commercial analysis and recommended concession

Aisha / Sam — reviewed the redline and the attached summary. Quick notes from Deal Desk: 

- Financial impact: If we grant a 15% ARR discount + accept an annual credit cap of 6 months, the net present value reduction vs. standard terms is approximately 18% over two years on the modeled ARR in VAL-7831. I’ve attached the spreadsheet.
- Exposure control: We should accept a capped remedy only if: (a) credit per incident is capped at 3 months of fees (customer proposed), (b) annual aggregate cap is 6 months (customer proposed), and (c) there is a hard limit on cumulative credits across the full term (we propose a final cumulative cap equal to 9 months).
- Operational safeguards: Ops must implement a failover routing policy to fallback-compatible model variants and enable aggressive prefix/KV caching to reduce blast radius. Also require a quarterly runbook review and a single tolerance window per year for any planned maintenance with prior notice.

Recommendation to Exec: Approve the concession under the following modified terms — 15% discount for a 24-month committed term with 6-month prepayment; accept customer's per-incident and annual caps with Redwood-proposed cumulative cap of 9 months; add standard exclusion for force majeure and customer-caused outages. This deviates from our standard max-credit policy and requires VP-level signoff.

Please approve or mark concerns.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Deal Desk — Redwood Inference
Attachment: VAL-7831-deal-summary.xlsx (xlsm, 72 KB)
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 11:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask — finance & margin check

Marissa — thanks for the analysis. Finance impact is acceptable if we close at scale, but margin compresses ~6 percentage points in year 1 assuming the 6-month prepay. We should get legal to tighten language around what counts as an incident (avoid multi-cause credits). Also recommend adding a graduated credit schedule (smaller credits for partial degradations) rather than all-or-nothing.

Looping in Jonas for operational approval on feasibility and for exec signoff for the policy deviation. If Jonas signs off, I’m comfortable recommending to the CFO for final acceptance.

Ben Carter
Sr. Director, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@valence.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: APPROVED: operational & executive concurrence (VAL-7831)

Team / Sam — after reviewing logs, risk modeling, and the proposed operational mitigations, I approve the recommended concession with the following final conditions: 

1) Accept 99.995% target with the customer-proposed per-incident cap (3 months) and annual cap (6 months) but limit cumulative liability to 9 months for the full 24-month term.
2) Require a technical annex that: (a) defines incident thresholds and credit calculations (graduated schedule per severity), (b) mandates multi-region active-active configuration for production workload within 90 days of go-live, and (c) requires Redwood to have automatic model-fallbacks and prefix caching enabled for Valence-specific routes.
3) Approve the commercial offset of a 15% ARR discount for a 24-month committed term with a 6-month prepayment. Legal to draft an amendment with explicit definitions and exclusions; Deal Desk to prepare final SOW & acceptance criteria.

This constitutes VP-level approval for deviation from standard credit exposure limits. Aisha / Marissa: proceed to execute paperwork and loop in Legal/Finance for signature. Ben: please prepare the finance approval pack for CFO. Sam: thanks for the clarity and the willingness to prepay. Looking forward to closing.

Jonas Weber
VP, Platform Operations — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
